content.value_statement: Complex Git maintenance can make history changes and conflict resolution difficult. This skill provides structured guidance, recovery steps, and an optional local helper for common advanced workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebasing, including reordering, squashing, editing, and aborting changes.
Guides conflict resolution with ours, theirs, manual merge tools, and continuation steps.
Provides workflows for branch cleanup, branch strategies, and stale branch review.
Describes reflog-based recovery and safe approaches to history rewriting.
Supports regression investigation with Git bisect and related troubleshooting guidance.
Includes an optional Bash helper for local repository maintenance tasks.
limitations: It cannot inspect, repair, or push repositories without user-approved local commands.
History rewrites can affect collaborators and require coordination before a force push.
The helper is designed for Bash and Git environments and may not fit every operating system.
Examples require adaptation to repository policies, protected branches, and team workflows.

use_cases.title: Clean a feature branch before review
use_cases.description: Turn a series of work-in-progress commits into a clear reviewable history with backups and rebase guidance.

use_cases.title: Resolve a difficult integration conflict
use_cases.description: Choose a resolution strategy, stage the correct files, and continue or abort a merge, rebase, or cherry-pick.

use_cases.title: Define a team branching model
use_cases.description: Compare Git Flow and trunk-based practices, then document rules for releases, hotfixes, and feature branches.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for a safe rebase
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to clean up my last five local commits before review. Give me a safe interactive rebase plan, including a backup step and how to abort.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a merge conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: I have conflicts while merging main into my feature branch. Help me inspect the conflict, decide between ours and theirs, and verify the result before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a lost commit
prompt_templates.prompt: I reset my branch and cannot find a recent commit. Give me a cautious reflog recovery workflow that avoids overwriting current work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a branch cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a branch cleanup procedure for our repository. Protect main and release branches, list candidates first, require confirmation before deletion, and include rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: I accidentally started a rebase and need to return to the original branch state.
output: Identify whether a rebase is active.
Create or confirm a backup reference if needed.
Run the documented abort action and check status afterward.

output_examples.input: Our feature branch has several commits that should become one reviewable change.
output: Create a backup branch before changing history.
Start an interactive rebase for the selected commits.
Mark related commits for squash, verify the final log, and coordinate before pushing rewritten history.

output_examples.input: We need to choose a branching strategy for frequent releases.
output: Compare trunk-based development and Git Flow against release cadence and team size.
Define protected branches and pull request requirements.
Document naming, cleanup, release, and hotfix procedures.

best_practices: Create a backup branch and inspect status before rewriting history or deleting branches.
Use force-with-lease only after coordinating with affected collaborators.
Review command targets and test recovery steps in a disposable repository first.
anti_patterns: Do not force push rewritten shared history without team agreement.
Do not bulk-delete branches before listing and reviewing the proposed targets.
Do not resolve conflicts by choosing ours or theirs without checking the intended behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically change my repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The optional helper runs only when you choose to execute it locally.

faq.question: Is interactive rebase safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: It can rewrite commit identifiers. Coordinate with collaborators and use a protected workflow before pushing changes.

faq.question: How can I recover a commit after a reset?
faq.answer: Use Git reflog to locate the prior reference, create a backup, and restore or branch from the selected commit.

faq.question: When should I use Git bisect?
faq.answer: Use it when you know a working and failing revision and need to locate the commit that introduced a regression.

faq.question: Can the helper delete branches or stashes?
faq.answer: Yes. Some helper actions modify local Git state after an interactive confirmation. Review the displayed targets first.

faq.question: Does the skill support Windows?
faq.answer: The documentation is broadly applicable, but the optional helper requires a Bash-compatible environment.
